text: Ghost is a Swedish rock band formed in Linköping in 2006. The band released their debut album, Opus Eponymous, in 2010, which earned them international recognition and reached number 50 on the Sverigetopplistan, earning a nomination for the 2011 Grammis Award for "Best Hard Rock" album. Their second album, Infestissumam, was released in early 2013 after initially facing delays due to US CD manufacturers rejecting the album's artwork, which was described as a "16th century illustration of an orgy"; the band used the regular edition's artwork for US deluxe pressings and released the album on 16 April. Infestissumam charted in seven countries, reached number one in Sweden, went gold, and won the Grammis and P3 Guld Awards for "Best Hard Rock/Metal Album" of 2013. Their third studio album, Meliora, was released on 21 August 2015 and reached number one in Sweden and number eight in the US. The band's fourth album, Prequelle, was released on 1 June 2018, with the single "Dance Macabre" released ahead of it on 17 May. Their fifth studio album, Impera, was released in 2022. The band's sixth studio album, Skeletá, was released in 2025 and became their first number one on the US Billboard 200 chart. Known for their costumed on-stage presence, Ghost's members except the lead vocalist are called "Nameless Ghouls," while the lead singer performs under the persona of "Papa Emeritus," a character with "demonic anti-pope" imagery, who changes for subsequent tours. The band's music combines hard rock, heavy metal, arena rock, and pop rock. In 2017, the identity of the lead singer was revealed to be Tobias Forge after former members Simon Söderberg, Mauro Rubino, Martin Hjertstedt, and Henrik Palm filed a legal action over royalties, claiming Forge withheld financial information and payments, and accused him of transforming Ghost into a solo project. Forge denied any legal partnership, stating the band was a solo project with musicians for hire. The single "Cirice" won the 2016 Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance. Ghost was formed when Tobias Forge wrote the song "Stand by Him," which he described as a "heavy metal riff" with a "Satanically-oriented lyric." He contacted his former Repugnant bandmate Gustaf Lindström to record it. In early 2008, the two recorded three songs: "Stand by Him," "Prime Mover," and "Death Knell," after which Forge decided to create an anonymous "theater band" inspired by horror films and Scandinavian metal traditions. He chose the name Ghost and initially intended to play guitar, offering the lead vocalist role to Messiah Marcolin, Mats Levén, Christer Göransson, and JB Christoffersson, all of whom declined, leading Forge to become the lead singer by default. On 12 March 2010, Forge posted the first three Ghost songs on MySpace, prompting record labels and managers to contact him. The band recorded their debut album in a basement studio in Linköping and released their first single, "Elizabeth," in June 2010. They played their first concert on 23 October 2010 at the Hammer of Doom festival in Würzburg, Germany. In 2011, they supported Paradise Lost on their "Draconian Times MMXI" tour and made their US debut at Maryland Deathfest on 29 May. They performed at the Download Festival in England on 11 June, where Phil Anselmo joined them on stage to perform "Bury Me In Smoke." In December 2011, they toured with Trivium, In Flames, Rise to Remain, and Insense. They began their first US tour, "13 Dates of Doom," in January 2012 and joined Mastodon and Opeth as opening acts on the Heritage Hunter Tour in April and May 2012. In June 2012, they won the "Breakthrough Band" award at the Metal Hammer Golden Gods Awards. In February 2012, a Nameless Ghoul confirmed the band had completed writing their second album. They recorded it in Nashville, Tennessee, with producer Nick Raskulinecz, and signed with Loma Vista Recordings in partnership with Republic Records. On 15 December 2012, they debuted "Secular Haze" in Linköping and released a cover of ABBA's "I'm a Marionette" with Dave Grohl. They introduced Papa Emeritus II at that show and announced Infestissumam's release in early 2013. On 5 February 2013, they changed their name to "Ghost B.C." in the US for legal reasons, explaining it was a pun on "Before Christ" but would be dropped by 2015. They toured Australia in February 2013 as part of the Soundwave Festival. In July 2013, they performed at the European Sonisphere Festival. In January 2014, they received six Loudwire Music Awards nominations. They toured Australia in January–February 2014 as part of the Big Day Out festival and embarked on the "Tour Year Zero" in April–May 2014. In July 2014, they performed at the European Sonisphere Festival. In 2015, Papa Emeritus II was "fired" and replaced by Papa Emeritus III, who was unveiled on 3 June 2015. The band promoted Meliora with a five-date acoustic tour called "Unholy/Unplugged" in the US, where Papa Emeritus III performed without his mitre and was accompanied by two guitarists and a kazoo player. A tour titled "Black to the Future" began on 22 September 2014 and ended on 1 November. In 2016, they released a new track "Square Hammer" on a radio show and an EP, Popestar, on 16 September, launching the Popestar Tour. After the North American tour ended on 12 November 2016, they toured Europe from late March to late April 2017. They opened for Iron Maiden on their 2017 North America tour from June to July 2017. A Nameless Ghoul stated they would write a darker album than Meliora, with Tobias confirming the fourth album would be released in 2018. In early 2017, the legal action against Forge revealed his identity. On 24 August 2017, they released the final music video from Meliora for "He Is." At the end of the Popestar Tour on 30 September 2017, Papa Emeritus III was dragged off stage, and a new character, Papa Nihil, was introduced as "Papa Emeritus Zero." They released their first live album, Ceremony and Devotion, digitally on 8 December 2017 and physically on 19 January 2018. On 13 April 2018, they released the single "Rats" and introduced Cardinal Copia as their new frontman, along with saxophonist Papa Nihil, expanding the band to a septet. Prequelle was released on 1 June 2018. They began the Rats! on the Road tour in the US from 5 May to 1 June and opened for Guns N' Roses in Oslo on 19 July 2018. They began the A Pale Tour Named Death in London on 9 September 2018, with a North American leg in the fall, and announced an early 2019 European tour on 10 September 2018. In March 2019, they performed in Australia and Japan at Download Festival. They were announced as the opening act for Metallica's WorldWired Tour from May to August 2019. A second North American tour with Nothing More was announced on 1 April 2019, and a European tour with All Them Witches and Tribulation on 8 July 2019. They released music videos for "Dance Macabre" on 17 October 2018 and "Faith" on 20 December 2018. In September 2019, they released the standalone single Kiss the Go-Goat / Mary on a Cross under the title Seven Inches of Satanic Panic, with a video for "Kiss the Go-Goat" released as "Chapter 8" of their web series. In an interview on 25 September 2019, Ghost confirmed no touring in 2020 except for one show in Mexico City on 3 March 2020, with the rest of the year dedicated to working on a new album expected for early 2021. At the final show of the Prequelle tour, they introduced Papa Emeritus IV as the next frontman. On 8 October 2020, they confirmed the release of their fifth studio album in winter 2020, with a tour planned for March 2021 postponed to fall 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. On the same day, they received the Music Export Prize of 2019 from the Swedish government. On 21 October 2020, they announced studio recording in January 2021 for a late 2021 release. On 30 December 2020, they announced "several big things" for 2021, indicating new music and live performances. Papa Emeritus IV made his public debut on 22 January 2021 on the Swedish game show "På spåret." They released a music video for "Life Eternal" on 3 March 2021, featuring footage from the Mexico City show. They became a featured artist on Metallica's tribute album The Metallica Blacklist, released on 10 September 2021, performing "Enter Sandman." On 30 September 2021, they unveiled the single "Hunter's Moon," featured on the soundtrack of the 2021 slasher film Halloween Kills. In an interview on 30 October 2021, Forge announced the album concept would be based on "the rise and fall of empires." On 20 January 2022, they released the single "Call Me Little Sunshine" as the second single from their fifth studio album.

Papa Emeritus IV made his public debut on the Swedish television game show "På spåret" on 22 January 2021, joining The Hellacopters to perform a cover of the Rolling Stones' "Sympathy for the Devil". Ghost released a music video for "Life Eternal" on 3 March 2021, featuring live footage from a previous show in Mexico City the year before. The band became a featured artist on Metallica's tribute album The Metallica Blacklist, released on 10 September 2021, where they performed "Enter Sandman". On 30 September 2021, Ghost unveiled their single "Hunter's Moon", which appears on the soundtrack of the 2021 slasher film Halloween Kills. In an interview on 30 October 2021, Forge announced that the upcoming album would be themed on "the rise and fall of empires". On 20 January 2022, the band released "Call Me Little Sunshine" as the second single from their fifth studio album, Impera, which was released on 11 March 2022. On 2 March 2022, they released the third single from the album, "Twenties". On 8 March, Ghost announced sponsorship of the JD Motorsports No. 4 Chevrolet Camaro SS driven by Bayley Currey at the 12 March NASCAR Xfinity Series race at Phoenix Raceway. The band performed "Call Me Little Sunshine" on Jimmy Kimmel Live! in a show that had been postponed due to touring commitments. On 27 July 2022, a music video for the album's fourth single, "Spillways", was released and was later rereleased in January 2023 with Joe Elliott as a featured guest. Ghost kicked off the Imperatour in the US from January to March 2022, co-headlining with Volbeat and Twin Temple. A European tour of the same name was announced on 23 November 2021, with Uncle Acid & the Deadbeats and Twin Temple as support. The band headlined Hellfest in Clisson, France on 18 June 2022. On 17 May 2022, they announced a second North American leg with Mastodon and Spiritbox as opening acts. In an interview on 12 September 2022, Forge confirmed more touring in 2023 and later revealed plans for Asia and Oceania, stating he was working on the follow-up to Impera. On 13 February 2023, the band announced a US tour from August to September 2023 with Amon Amarth as special guests. On 1 February 2023, they hosted an archival exhibition in Los Angeles celebrating their "1969 era", which included Papa Nihil and other items from that time. After the release of Chapter 16 in their web series, speculation arose that Papa Emeritus IV would be "killed off" at the end of the Imperatour following the announcement of a second show at the Kia Forum in Inglewood. A South American leg was announced on 4 April 2023, marking the band's first headlining shows in Brazil and Argentina, following reports of new music to be released before their second European leg. Prior to the second Europe leg, the band released their fourth EP, Phantomime, a covers EP supported by a single of their cover of Genesis' "Jesus He Knows Me", originally scheduled for 18 May 2023 but postponed to 19 May. Ghost collaborated with actor Patrick Wilson and released a single of their cover of Shakespears Sister's "Stay" on 7 July 2023, featured in the 2023 film Insidious: The Red Door. On 7 September 2023, the band received its first platinum certification for the single "Mary On A Cross" from their EP Seven Inches of Satanic Panic. After South American performances, the Imperatour concluded in October 2023 with three shows in Australia, with the Brisbane performance on 7 October 2023 being the final show to feature Papa Emeritus IV. On 11 October 2023, Forge confirmed that a Ghost movie was in development, noting that the Inglewood performances in September 2023 were filmed. On 1 December 2023, Ghost released a compilation album titled 13 Commandments, marking the global streaming release of Meliora Redux's exclusive track "Zenith", previously only available on physical formats. In an interview with Metal Hammer on 9 December 2023, Forge confirmed work on the next studio album had begun, stating a few songs had been written, and later acknowledged in a New Year's message that there was "lots to come" in 2024. On 4 April 2024, the band released a teaser for the movie without naming it, depicting Papa Emeritus IV on stage and announcing a worldwide release. The film was later revealed to be titled Rite Here Rite Now, released on 20 June 2024. A single, "The Future Is a Foreign Land", was released on 21 June 2024, a day after the film. The movie's soundtrack was released on 26 July 2024 through Loma Vista Recordings. On 28 October 2024, the band announced a then-untitled world tour beginning in 2025, later named the "Skeletour", starting with a European leg from 15 April to 24 May, followed by a North American leg from 9 July to 16 August, concluding in Mexico City on 25 September. The band confirmed additional dates would be announced. On 5 February 2025, Papa V Perpetua was revealed as the new frontman for Ghost. A month later, the band released the single "Satanized" with a music video and announced the title of their sixth studio album, Skeletá, released on 25 April 2025. The album's second single, "Lachryma", was released on 11 April 2025, and the third single, "Peacefield", on 22 April 2025. A music video for "Peacefield" was released on 28 April 2025. In May 2025, the album topped the Billboard 200, accumulating 86,000 equivalent album units. On 26 September 2025, the band revealed that the two Mexico City shows were filmed for a future concert film. On 29 September 2025, a second North American leg for the Skeletour was announced for January to February 2026. In November 2025, "Lachryma" was nominated for Best Metal Performance at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards. On 16 January 2026, the band officially released their cover of "It's a Sin" by Pet Shop Boys to streaming services, originally included as a bonus track on their 2018 album Prequelle. Ghost's music spans genres including hard rock, heavy metal, arena rock, pop rock, doom metal, progressive rock, psychedelic rock, occult rock, shock rock, symphonic metal, and gothic rock. Adrien Begrand of PopMatters noted Ghost's early sounds recall Black Sabbath, Pentagram, and Judas Priest, as well as the progressive and psychedelic rock of the late '60s. A Nameless Ghoul described Ghost as a black metal band in the traditional sense but said they do not fit current black metal norms, describing their music as a mix of pop and death metal. A Nameless Ghoul stated their influences range from classic rock to extreme underground metal bands of the '80s to film scores and emotional harmonic music. The Swedish and Scandinavian black metal movement of the early '90s plays a major role in their act, and each member has a metal background. However, the band has repeatedly stated they do not aim to be a metal band. For their second album, Ghost adopted a more diverse songwriting style, with each song having its own signature. Only a few members write songs; they compose an acoustic outline before adding instrumentation to create a group sound rather than a guitar-dominated one. In 2017, Forge claimed he was the main author of every song except "Year Zero" and "Zenith", which were Persner's ideas. Forge explained that to maintain Ghost's sound despite lineup changes, he teaches the members to play like him, noting he is a good guitarist but only an "okay" drummer, bassist, and keyboardist, so he ensures they "underperform [laughs] together". Their lyrics are often Satanic; one Ghoul described Infestissumam as about the arrival of the Devil in biblical terms, similar to doomsday, and that Infestissumam deals with the presence of the Devil and Antichrist. The band has consistently stated their image is tongue-in-cheek and that they have no militant agenda, calling themselves an entertainment group. They use humor during shows, and Infestissumam explores themes of how people relate to deities, submission, superstition, and religious horrors. A Nameless Ghoul said the second album addresses how men throughout history have deemed women as the Devil, citing the Inquisition as an example. The group's theatrics are influenced by Kiss, David Bowie, and Alice Cooper, though a member cited Pink Floyd as a major influence. A Ghoul cited Death SS as an influence on their "gimmick" but not their music. Ghost's Satanic theme has caused issues in the US; while recording Infestissumam in Nashville, they could not find choral singers and recorded the parts in Hollywood. They were unable to find a US record manufacturer due to nudity in the artwork, causing a release delay. When asked if their music had become more "radio-friendly", a Nameless Ghoul responded that mainstream America banned their music from major chain stores, late-night TV, and commercial radio, saying "So, yes, mainstream America is absolutely welcoming us with open legs". During an October 2015 interview, a band member stated that by 2015 the US had become more accepting, evidenced by their appearance as main musical guests on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert on 30 October 2015 during a Halloween-themed episode, their first live US television appearance. Chicago restaurant Kuma's Corner added a "The Ghost" hamburger to its menu, including goat shoulder, red wine reduction, and a communion wafer. A Catholic food blogger acknowledged the wafer is a mockery of something holy, and the restaurant owner respected religion while refusing to remove the burger, citing the First Amendment and donating $1,500 to Catholic Charities of the Chicago Archdiocese. The members of Ghost mimic the Roman Catholic Church but reverse the image to worship Satan instead of the Holy Trinity. From 2010 to 2017, the Nameless Ghouls represented the five elements: lead guitarist (fire), bassist (water), keyboardist (wind), drummer (earth), and rhythm guitarist (ether), each wearing their alchemical symbol on their instrument. With Meliora, each Ghoul had all five elemental symbols embroidered on the right breast of their costumes, with the individual symbol highlighted. In 2018, the lineup expanded to include a third guitarist, two female keyboardists called the "Ghoulettes", and Papa Nihil on saxophone. The group's vocalist portrays the Satanic priest character Papa Emeritus. There have been four versions of Papa Emeritus: the second was introduced on 12 December 2012 in Linköping; on 3 June 2015, the second Papa Emeritus welcomed his younger brother, Papa Emeritus III, after being "fired" for failing to overthrow governments and churches; Papa Emeritus II and III had a 3-month age difference. On 30 September 2017, during a Gothenburg show, Papa Emeritus III was dragged off stage by two men, who escorted a new character, Papa Emeritus 0, to the stage. Papa Emeritus 0 is portrayed as significantly older, using a walker and oxygen tank. On 19 January 2018, a video showed a character, implied to be Papa Emeritus IV, listening to Ceremony and Devotion on 8-track tape while critiquing Papa Emeritus III's vocals, with his face hidden but wearing red vestments similar to a cardinal priest. He was later revealed to be Cardinal Copia. At the final show of the Prequelle tour, Papa Nihil "died" and Cardinal Copia became Papa Emeritus IV. Papa Nihil was later resurrected during the European leg of the Imperatour. In March 2025, the band announced Papa V Perpetua as their next frontman. All versions of Papa Emeritus are actually the same vocalist, Tobias Forge. Peter Hällje, a former bandmate of Martin Persner, claimed he designed the Papa Emeritus character in 2005 before Ghost's formation and agreed to let Persner use it. This claim was later confirmed by Forge. In April 2018, it was revealed that Cardinal Copia would be the "new leader", making his live debut at a private acoustic show on 6 April; he is not part of the Papa Emeritus lineage. Forge described Copia as "not the boss" but as a "toastmaster", junior to a pope, and stated that Papa Emeritus Zero (Papa Nihil) was passing on and needed to teach Copia to become a pope and earn his skull paint. Copia's costume consists of cardinal vestments or a black or white tuxedo, with a prosthetic mask featuring black eye makeup and multi-colored eyes. In promotion for their 2018 US tour, a video showed Papa Emeritus I through III being killed and embalmed. In an interview the following month, Forge stated that unlike previous frontmen, Cardinal Copia was planned to last about five years. The band also welcomed Papa Nihil, the first band member besides Forge to serve in that role.

Cardinal Copia made his live debut with Ghost at a private acoustic show on 6 April and is not part of the Papa Emeritus lineage; Forge described him as "the toastmaster," not the boss, noting that a cardinal is junior to a pope, and that Papa Emeritus Zero (a.k.a. Papa Nihil) is still active but passing on, needing to teach Copia to earn his skull paint. Copia's costume includes either cardinal vestments or a black or white tuxedo, along with a prosthetic mask featuring black eye makeup and multi-colored eyes, similar to prior Papa Emeritus characters. In a 2018 US tour promotional video, Papa Emeritus I through III were shown as killed and embalmed; Forge later stated that, unlike previous frontmen, Cardinal Copia is intended to last about five years. Papa Nihil, introduced as the first band member besides Forge to receive a character name, is the ancestor of all Papa Emeritus characters and remains the only surviving member of that lineage after the "deaths" of his descendants. During the final show of the Prequelle tour, Cardinal Copia was "elevated" to become Papa Emeritus IV. Ghost has long maintained anonymity, with members prior to 2017 not publicly revealing their names and the five instrumentalists referred to as "Nameless Ghouls"; they sign merchandise with alchemical symbols, while Papa Emeritus signs with his stage name or "P.E." One Ghoul clarified that anonymity was not to gain attention but to remove individual personalities and let audiences focus on the artwork, adding that without the music's energy, fans would not have been drawn to their appearance. In 2011, a Nameless Ghoul noted they were often mistaken for roadies, even being ejected from venues due to forgotten backstage passes. In early 2012, a member expressed enjoyment in being an individual and stated they could step outside the group's bubble. In May 2013, a Ghoul revealed they had begun sharing their membership with local friends and family for "house peace." In an August 2013 interview with Jack Osbourne, a member claimed Dave Grohl had dressed as a Nameless Ghoul and secretly performed with Ghost. In April 2014, a Nameless Ghoul confirmed that the band has had several member changes over the years. The Swedish Performing Rights Society reportedly credited Tobias Forge, vocalist of Subvision and Repugnant and former guitarist for Crashdïet (using the alias Mary Goore), as "A Ghoul Writer" for all Ghost songs, leading to speculation that Forge was Papa Emeritus; ASCAP's database confirmed Forge's authorship when searched, though the songs are listed under the pseudonym. Ghost initially refused to comment on identity rumors. In March 2017, Martin Persner of Magna Carta Cartel claimed he was the rhythm guitarist (Omega) from 2009 to July 2016, marking the first public identification of a Ghost member. A few months prior, the band recruited a new bassist suspected to be Megan Thomas, later confirmed by Forge. A 2017 lawsuit against Forge revealed the names of four past members and several others; Forge stated that Ghost has always been a "Bathory sort of band" where live performers were not necessarily the same as those on recordings. The lawsuit was dismissed on 17 October 2018. Ghost's live performances feature characters rather than real individuals, with the singer currently being "Papa V Perpetua" and the rest officially known as "Nameless Ghouls," though roles are categorized by elemental themes—fire, earth, water, air, and aether—originally marked by symbol patches on stage outfits. With the 2018 Prequelle tour cycle, the live lineup expanded to seven ghouls, making the elemental symbols obsolete. Ghost generally does not publicly identify ghouls through official channels, though in recent years they have become more open about such information. Due to long-standing NDAs, active members are prohibited from discussing their involvement publicly, though the fanbase quickly deduces identities once members appear on stage.
